method.start: Immediately before fetch; request options, timeout setup, guards and initial report write/fsync occur beforehand.
method.headers: Immediately after fetch resolves with response headers.
method.complete: Immediately after the response body reader reaches done, before JSON parsing, hashing or final report writes.
method.requests: Both fetch promises launched in the same process and awaited together; no additional endpoints or retry.
method.responseProcessing: Raw bounded bodies retained in memory; JSON parsing, sanitization and hashing occur only after both requests settle.

limitations: Both services have already been accessed during publication verification. This single observation does not establish cold or warm state.
One sample per endpoint, not percentiles, a controlled before/after experiment or a guaranteed user latency.
Client-observed elapsed time still combines local scheduling and HTTP client work, network, CDN/platform and server stages; these stages are not individually instrumented.
Direct Render and Netlify proxy are different paths. Their difference cannot by itself be attributed solely to Function/proxy execution.
Node starts the two asynchronous fetch calls successively in the same turn; they overlap, but their initiation timestamps are not exactly simultaneous.
